rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 RULES 1.1 TURN ACTIONS 1.2 GAME END 1.3 FINAL SCORE 2 WORKER TILE COUNTS 2.1 2 players: 2.2 3 players: 2.3 4 players: 3 JUNGLE TILE OVERVIEW 4 2 player game RULES TURN ACTIONS 1) Place 1 worker tile from your hand of 3 tiles. May rotate freely, but may not place next to another worker tile. Note: Once the draw pile and display of jungle tiles are empty, you may choose to spend 1 sun token per turn to overbuild one of your own worker tiles instead. Each worker tile spot may only be overbuilt once. 2) For each open spot with 2 adjacent worker tiles: place 1 jungle tile from the face-up display. 3) Activate workers at each shared edge between newly placed tiles (jungle or worker) and their adjacent tiles. For each worker (even those belonging to other players), the action on the adjacent tile is performed once. Note: Resources/points are always distributed to the player who owns the worker, even if activated during another player's turn. 4) Draw 1 worker tile to your hand, if possible. 5) Refill jungle tile display, if possible. GAME END The game ends when all players have placed their last worker tile. FINAL SCORE For each temple: the player with the most adjacent workers receives 6 gold. The player with the second-most adjacent workers receives 3 gold. If tied for first place: divide 6 gold between the tied players and do not award second place. If tied for second place: divide 3 gold among the tied players, rounding down. If only one player is at the temple, they earn 6 gold and no one receives second place. Score 1 point for each gold collected. Score 1 point for each remaining sun token. Score points for each player's water scoring track. Tiebreaker: most cacao fruit remaining WORKER TILE COUNTS 2 players: 4x 1-1-1-1 5x 2-1-0-1 1x 3-0-0-1 1x 3-1-0-0 3 players: 3x 1-1-1-1 5x 2-1-0-1 1x 3-0-0-1 1x 3-1-0-0 4 players: 3x 1-1-1-1 4x 2-1-0-1 1x 3-0-0-1 1x 3-1-0-0 JUNGLE TILE OVERVIEW Plantations : Take the indicated cacao per worker, up to your maximum storage of 5. (8 total tiles: 6 single, 2 double) (2 player game: 4 single, 2 double) Markets : Sell 1 cacao per worker at the indicated price. (7 total tiles: 2x2 gold, 4x3 gold, 1x4 gold) (2 player game: 7 total tiles: 2x2 gold, 4x3 gold, 1x4 gold Gold Mines : Take the indicated gold per worker. (3 total tiles: 2x1 gold, 1x2 gold) Water : Move your water carrier forward one space per worker. (3 total tiles) Sun Worshipping Sites : Take 1 sun token per worker, up to your maximum of 3. These can be spent to overbuild your own worker tiles late in the game, or are worth 1 point at game end. (2 total tiles) Temples : No immediate effect. At game end, each temple is scored separately. For each temple, the player with the most adjacent workers receives 6 gold, and second most receives 3 gold. If tied for first place: divide 6 gold between the tied players and do not award second place. If tied for second place: divide 3 gold among the tied players, rounding down. If only one player is at the temple, they earn 6 gold and no one receives second place. (5 total tiles) Note: Some tiles are removed in a 2-player game. See below 2 player game All tiles perform the same way as above. After tiles are removed, you are left with the following to play with: Plantations : (6 total tiles: 4 single, 2 double) Markets : (6 total tiles: 2x2 gold, 3x3 gold, 1x4 gold) Gold Mines : (2 total tiles: 1x1 gold, 1x2 gold) Water : (2 total tiles) Sun Worshipping Sites : (1 total tile) Temples : (4 total tiles)

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Tile laying game of resource conversion. Didn't left a memory in my head. Other than the usual competition for spaces, there's not much player interaction.

[Rating: 2/10] rate a 3 for being mostly luck, then subtract a point for being a design so lazy that it fails to compensate player 1 for the obvious fact he gets screwed on his first move.

[Rating: 2/10] It feels like carcassonne, although with much fewer options to place your tiles. Lots of randomness, and not a lot of replayability.

[Rating: 2/10] Abstract, dry, little player interactive, no depth -> no replayability, can't relate to the theme.. For 2015 not a game well done

[Rating: 2/10] Mweh, couldn't really care for it. Not really bad, but not that special either, a lot of other tile layers I'd rather play (carcassonne, Kingdomino Origins). This gets to the point that it is so light, the decision space gets too limited and there isn't a lot of tension, as most options seem 'okay'. Probably a great game to play with kids though.

[Rating: 2/10] Conceptually, I love it. In practice, however, decisions were limited and disappointingly straightforward (i.e., the 'best choice' on any given turn was generally obvious and unequivocal). I have an admiration for the main mechanic—"workers" as "tiles"—and will happily play a game if offered. Just wish the cache of tile actions was a bit larger and/or more interesting.

[Rating: 3/10] Shocked at the high ratings this game is getting. Yes, it's a good game, looks nice and reminds one of Carcassonne. But there just isn't much there. After a handful of plays I just don't see a lot replayability.   Edit: Just played King Chocolate which came out around the same time. It's in the 3000 range while this is now in the top 500.  Sometimes I think BGGers are crazy and this is one such time.  Quite bluntly, I think this game sucks in comparison.

[Rating: 3/10] It was a cute little game to play with my little sister, but not complicated enough to keep my interest otherwise.
